convention: Equirectangular 2:1. Left edge = 180 deg W (-180), centre = 0 deg longitude (prime meridian), top = +90 deg (north). East longitude increases to the right. With three.js SphereGeometry default UVs (+Y = north pole), u=0.5 (lon 0) lies on +X and u=0.75 (90E) on -Z, so east = positive rotation about +Y (prograde). Apply the body's own prime-meridian angle W(t) as a rotation about +Y.

milkyway.frame: Celestial (equatorial, ICRF/J2000), plate carree. Image centre = RA 0h, dec 0; RA increases to the LEFT (sky seen from inside); top = +90 dec. Pixel x -> RA = (0.5 - x/W) * 360 deg mod 360; y -> dec = 90 - y/H*180. Verified: LMC lands at RA~80 deg, dec~-69.
